text: 38 C.F.R. Sec. 14.636 defines reimbursable 'expenses' as nonrecurring expenses incurred directly in prosecuting a claim, with examples that include copies of medical records from outside sources and the cost of an expert witness or an expert opinion.

text: 38 C.F.R. Sec. 14.636 sets factors for challenging expenses as excessive or unreasonable, including case complexity, potential extent of benefits recoverable, and whether travel expenses match those normally incurred by other representatives.
notes: NO fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS failure on every URL). Lead source IDs (all unfetched): DS2. Implies an expense passed through must be reasonable relative to recoverable benefits.

text: INTERPRETATION: A per-file CUE/effective-date review bought by an accredited representative for a specific claimant's matter could plausibly be passed through as a 'nonrecurring expense incurred directly in the prosecution of a claim' (by analogy to 'expert opinion'), whereas a per-seat SaaS subscription would more likely be treated as normal overhead.
notes: NO fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS failure on every URL). Lead source IDs (all unfetched): DS2, DS21, DS22.
